intro: Excerpts copied from the live Claude Manager workspace (C:\APPS\CLAUDE) and its companion hook scripts in C:\Users\renne\.claude. Each shows the real code behind an orchestration, supervision, hook, or automation capability. Registry-driven throughout — paths and ports come from C:\QIH\ecosystem\qi_registry.json, never hardcoded.

snippets.title: Agent definition front-matter + role
snippets.code:
---
name: hive-architect
description: Strategic system designer for QI Hive. Use for architecture
  decisions, multi-project design, choosing patterns, breaking-change
  analysis, ADRs, and implementation plans before code is written.
  NOT for writing code — design only. Hand off to hive-builder.
model: opus
tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch
---

You are the **QI Hive Architect**. You design systems before anyone builds them.
...
You are the most expensive model in the team. Use deep reasoning. Do not generate code.
snippets.explanation: Every hive-* agent is a Markdown file whose YAML front-matter pins three things the harness reads: the model tier (Opus here — reserved for design), the exact tools the agent may use (the architect is read-only + web; no Write/Edit), and the description the dispatcher matches against. The body is the role prompt. Eight such files (architect, builder, inspector, ops, scout, scribe, tester, librarian) make up the fabric.

snippets.title: Builder hardcodes the QI conventions
snippets.feature: Convention enforcement at the agent level
snippets.code:
## QI conventions you must respect
- Ports: pull from `C:\QIH\ecosystem\qi_registry.json` — never hardcode a port from memory.
- File paths: raw strings `r"C:\..."` in Python.
- Encoding: always `encoding="utf-8"`. On stdout: `sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")`.
- Scripts: write to `.py` files; never use bash heredocs (encoding breaks).
- Services: NSSM service names ALWAYS prefixed `QI_` (e.g., `QI_MapSnap`).
- Logs go to `<project>\LOGS\` — never the project root.

## When to hand off
- After implementation: dispatch to `hive-inspector` for review before merging.
snippets.explanation: The builder agent doesn't just say 'write code' — it bakes the QI Standards into the prompt so every sub-agent run produces compliant output (registry ports, raw-string paths, UTF-8, QI_ service prefix, logs in LOGS\). It also encodes the workflow contract: after building, hand off to the inspector. This is how the fabric keeps standards without the main thread re-stating them each time.

snippets.title: The dispatcher principle
snippets.feature: Dispatch discipline — main thread is the orchestrator
snippets.code:
## Core principle

I am the **dispatcher**, not the doer of everything. Each task type below has
an agent. If a sub-task fits a role, I dispatch via the `Agent` tool with
`subagent_type=hive-<role>`. I do not do the work in the main thread when there
is an agent for it.

Exceptions: trivial single-step tasks (one Edit, one Bash command, answering a
factual question). For anything multi-step, dispatch.

## Standard workflows
### Workflow A — design + implement + ship
1. **hive-architect** (Opus) — design the change. Output: implementation plan.
2. **hive-builder** (Sonnet) — execute the plan. Output: code on disk.
3. **hive-inspector** (Sonnet) — review the change. Output: findings.
4. If inspector found issues: back to **hive-builder** with the findings.
5. **hive-scribe** (Haiku) — write session summary at end.
snippets.explanation: Claude Code does not auto-route to sub-agents — the protocol is explicit that 'if I don't dispatch, no one does.' This file is the operating rule the main thread follows: a trigger->agent table plus chained workflows (design->build->review->document). It is what turns eight inert .md files into an actual multi-agent operating mode, with anti-patterns (never bypass the inspector, never fake attribution, keep delegation one level deep) spelled out below.

snippets.title: Registry walk — the main loop
snippets.code:
reg = json.loads(REGISTRY.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
projects = reg.get("projects", [])
report = {"generated_at": now_iso(), "projects": []}
for p in projects:
    print(f"[supervisor] inspecting {p['id']} at {p['path']} ...")
    try:
        report["projects"].append(inspect_project(p))
    except Exception as exc:
        report["projects"].append({"id": p["id"], "name": p.get("name", p["id"]),
                                    "path": p.get("path"), "severity": "red",
                                    "findings": [{"severity": "red", "kind": "supervisor_error",
                                                  "msg": f"inspector exception: {exc}"}]})

OUT_REPORT.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
OUT_DASHBOARD.write_text(render_dashboard(report), encoding="utf-8")
feed_qih_status(report)
snippets.explanation: The supervisor's spine: read the single ecosystem registry, inspect every registered project, and emit three artifacts — report.json (machine), DASHBOARD.md (human), and a feed into C:\QIH\data\status.json (the Hive dashboard panels). The per-project try/except is deliberate: an inspector exception on one project becomes a red finding for that project, never a crash that loses the whole scan.

snippets.title: Per-project drift inspection
snippets.feature: Drift detection — git, services, tasks, keepalive
snippets.code:
# Git
gs = git_state(path)
result["git"] = gs
if gs.get("status") == "dirty":
    sev = "yellow" if (gs["untracked"] + gs["modified"]) <= 5 else "red"
    result["findings"].append({"severity": sev, "kind": "git_dirty",
        "msg": f"{gs['untracked']} untracked, {gs['modified']} modified"})
if (gs.get("last_commit_age_days") or 0) > 14:
    result["findings"].append({"severity": "yellow", "kind": "stale_commits",
        "msg": f"Last commit was {gs['last_commit_age_days']} days ago"})

# Services
svcs = list_services_for(str(path))
for s in svcs:
    if s.get("Status") != "Running":
        result["findings"].append({"severity": "red", "kind": "service_down",
            "msg": f"Service {s['Name']} is {s['Status']}"})

result["severity"] = severity_for(result)
snippets.explanation: What 'drift' concretely means. For each project the supervisor checks git cleanliness (>5 dirty files escalates yellow->red), commit staleness (>14 days), keepalive failure files, QI_ NSSM service state (anything not Running is red), and scheduled-task exit codes. Each becomes a severity-tagged finding; severity_for() rolls them into the project's red/yellow/green.

snippets.title: Finding the project's QI_ services via NSSM
snippets.feature: Service drift — only services rooted under the project
snippets.explanation: The supervisor shells into PowerShell to attribute services to projects correctly: for every Windows service it asks nssm.exe for the Application and AppDirectory, and only counts a service as belonging to a project if one of those paths is rooted under the project's registered path. That way a stopped QI_ service is reported against the right project, not guessed by name.

snippets.title: Hook + permission wiring
snippets.explanation: This project's harness config does two jobs. permissions.defaultMode=bypassPermissions (plus the explicit allow list) is why a management session never stops to ask before running Bash/Edit/MCP. The hooks block wires SessionEnd and SubagentStop to fire the two inbox scripts via the pinned Python interpreter with a 15s timeout. (SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit are wired in the global ~/.claude config, not here.)

snippets.title: SessionStart — Brain probe that fails LOUD
snippets.explanation:
The SessionStart hook injects the ecosystem briefing AND a live Brain probe. The design choice is to fail LOUD: if Brain is unreachable, the injected context explicitly tells Claude the session is degraded and forbids pretending qi.* calls succeeded — so memory integrity can't be silently lost. Note the probe still targets :9010, the pre-2026-05-14 port; Brain now lives on :9011, which is why this is flagged on the roadmap.  

_Note: this excerpt is sanitised — identifiers naming the owner have been replaced with a generic term, per the project rule that no real person's name appears in documentation. The underlying source is unchanged._

snippets.title: Inferring the project from cwd
snippets.feature: Every session leaves a trace — correct project attribution
snippets.explanation: Both inbox hooks decide which project a session belongs to by longest-prefix matching the current working directory against every registered project path (longest match wins, so C:\APPS\NAYA\filehq beats C:\APPS\NAYA). Anything under C:\APPS\CLAUDE — including ephemeral worktrees — falls through to claude_manager. This is what lets the SessionEnd stub be filed under the right project in qi_brain.db without Claude stating it.

snippets.title: Normalising a sub-agent name to its Hive role
snippets.explanation: When a sub-agent finishes, the SubagentStop hook has to record WHO did the work. Different harness versions name the agent field differently, so it tries four keys, strips any hive-/hive_ prefix, and — if the bare name is a known Hive role — normalises to a canonical hive_<role> id. That id is written into the inbox stub so qi_brain.db attributes the work to the right specialist instead of a generic 'subagent'.

snippets.title: Building the kill-set — without touching services
snippets.feature: Clean-restart guard — orphaned MCP trees only
snippets.explanation: The fix for Claude Desktop's 'file in use' restart failure. It maps the whole process tree, then targets two things: every claude.exe descendant tree, and orphaned MCP-signature processes (sqlite/git/brain/peers stdio servers) whose parent Claude is gone. Is-UnderService excludes anything parented by services.exe/nssm/svchost, so the QI_ tunnels and the Brain API are never collateral — and it removes its own ancestor chain so running it from inside a session can't kill the host.

snippets.title: Only ever auto-fix what is provably safe
snippets.explanation: The self-audit's guiding rule: --apply-safe only removes a git worktree if its working tree is completely clean (no uncommitted changes), so no work is ever destroyed. A dirty or numerous worktree is not touched — it's pushed onto needs_decision for the in-session review gate. The same split (auto_fixed vs needs_decision) governs orphan kills and .claude.json pruning; risky items are always reported, never auto-applied.

snippets.title: Audit -> notify -> open the decision gate
snippets.code:
# 1. audit + safe auto-fix
$summary = & $py "$tool\qi_self_audit.py" "--apply-safe" 2>&1 | Out-String
$head = ($summary -split "`n" | Where-Object { $_ -match "^AUDIT " } | Select-Object -First 1)
$decisions = ($summary -split "`n" | Where-Object { $_ -match "DECISION:" }).Count
$msg = "QI Monthly Self-Audit ($ts)`n$head`n$decisions item(s) need your decision. " +
       "Open Claude and say 'monthly audit' to review."
# 2. notify via Tasuke
& $py "$tool\qi_tasuke_notify.py" $msg 2>&1 | Add-Content $log
# 3. auto-open Claude Desktop
Start-Process "shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude"
snippets.explanation: The body of the QI_ClaudeSelfAudit task (last Friday of the month). It runs the audit with safe auto-fixes, parses the one-line AUDIT summary and the DECISION count out of stdout, sends the owner a LINE heads-up via Tasuke, then auto-launches Claude Desktop. The launch matters: the SessionStart hook sees PENDING_REVIEW.json and presents the decision gate before any new work — closing the loop from cron to human review.

snippets.title: Register projects + refresh recorded state
snippets.feature: Keep the Brain in sync with reality
snippets.code:
db = sqlite3.connect(r"C:\QIH\data\qi_brain.db")
cur = db.cursor()

# Step 1: register new projects (idempotent)
for p in new_projects:
    cur.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO projects VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)", p)
cur.execute("UPDATE projects SET api_port=9011 WHERE project_id='qi_brain'")

# Step 2: refresh project_state for all projects
for pid, phase, status, summary, blockers, nxt in states:
    cur.execute(
        "INSERT INTO project_state (project_id, agent_id, phase, status, summary, "
        "blockers, next_steps, recorded_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
        (pid, AGENT, phase, status, summary, blockers, nxt, NOW))

# Step 3: merge bad project IDs in session_log
cur.execute("UPDATE session_log SET project_id='openclaw' WHERE project_id='OpenClaw'")
db.commit()
snippets.explanation: A reconciliation pass operating directly on qi_brain.db — the Brain's SQLite store. It registers projects the Brain didn't know yet (INSERT OR IGNORE so re-runs are safe), corrects stale fields (qi_brain's own port to 9011 after the 9010 move), writes a fresh project_state row for every project from observed git/service reality, and merges mislabelled session_log rows (OpenClaw -> the canonical lowercase openclaw). This is how the management workspace makes the Brain's memory match what actually happened on disk.

snippets.title: Composing the injected session context
snippets.explanation: The SessionStart hook's payload. It concatenates four blocks — the ecosystem briefing (MEMORY.md + rules + user profile via qi_context_loader), the live Brain status block, the Hive dispatch reminder (roles + DISPATCH_PROTOCOL.md path), and the monthly-audit gate if one is pending — then emits them as additionalContext under hookSpecificOutput. Claude Code injects that string into the session so the model wakes up already knowing the whole QI landscape and the dispatch rule before the first user message.
